questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The language spoken there.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite difficult. But got an email with an online pamphlet with some useful information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was really really difficult. The university doesn't help you so you have to do it all on your own.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Most people live off campus so it's not a problem.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I chose some courses for my learning agreement before I went on exchange and when I then arrived at the university I realized that most of these courses didn't exist anymore or I wasn't allowed to register for them. So I had to choose all new courses.
I didn't know when registration would open and kept waiting for further information about the course registration process which I never got. So had to figure it out on my own. Many of the courses I wanted to attend I wasn't allowed to apply for. So there were very few courses I could choose and most of these were only 3 ECTS. Så quite difficult to find courses to do 30 ECTS in total. And difficult to find courses that didn't overlap. And didn't really get any help.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You can register for as many courses as you want to and you can change your registrations after the classes have already started. And then at the end of the semester you register for the exams you want to take.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much but the Erasmus coordinator gave some really good advice.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the courses I applied for but it was very few courses I was allowed to apply for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask the Erasmus coordinator for help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took BA and MA courses. The level was not too difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style was pretty much the same.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Methods in Protein Biochemistry
Lab Course Molecular Biology and Biochemistry
German as a Foreign Language B1.1 plus B1.2
Biology and Diagnostics of Pathogenic Bacteria - an Introduction
English - English in Science and Technology C1
Plant and Animal Cell Biology
English - Writing Academic Research Papers C2

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: German language courses. Gives ECTS and it's really useful to learn the language/improve it.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Travelling around Germany.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
The food cost pretty much the same as at home.
But very cheap beer and alcohol:)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Sign up for Hochschulsport. It costs 10 Euros and then you can sign up for as many sports classes as you want to.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Lots of different kinds of sports (Hochschulsport). 
And Language Cafe once a week where you could meet other students (mainly international students).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do sports. It's nice to get exercise and a good way to make friends and get to know students that aren't international students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Download the ESN TUMi app and then you can sign up for lots of events and excursions with other international students.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Very easy. 
Just need to drink beer instead of wine.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Learn to speak German. 
Live with German students.
Avoid spending a lot of time with people from your home country.
Sign up for Hochschulsport.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Everything was very disorganized and random. I missed structure.
And everything was on paper instead of online and a bit more old-fashioned.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The beer:)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Learn some German before you go on exchange.
Sign up for the Buddy Program.
Get ready to drink a lot of very good beer:)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: wg-gesucht is a good place to find housing.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Meeting lots of sweet people and experiencing many new things. I was never bored. And meeting people from all over the world.
And improving my German.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
That the university was so disorganized and helped me so little. 
(finding housing, registering for courses)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
